modules.title: Pronunciation & Fluency — English Foundation
modules.reason: Build clear, understandable English speech before pushing harder on speaking content.
modules.checkpoint: Follow the playlist in order and complete the daily routine on at least 5 days.

items.title: 1. Shadowing — speak with the model
items.description: English with Lucy: learn the shadowing method, then copy the speaker's rhythm, phrasing and pronunciation.

items.title: 2. Connected speech — linking and missing sounds
items.description: BBC Learning English: practise how natural English links sounds and reduces them in connected speech.

items.title: 3. Schwa — the most common English vowel sound
items.description: BBC Learning English: practise the schwa so unstressed syllables sound more natural and easier to produce.

items.title: 4. Build fluency naturally at home
items.description: English with Lucy: use shadowing, enjoyable input, repetition and regular English exposure to build fluency.

items.title: Daily speaking routine
items.description: Do 10 minutes of shadowing, 5–10 minutes of clear speaking or Read Aloud, then record one short response and listen back. Check only: Can I understand every word? Is my pace natural? Am I pausing naturally? If yes, then push for more content.

items.title: Natural English every day
items.description: Spend regular time with English you actually enjoy—movies, series, YouTube, podcasts, work conversations or reading. Do not pause every sentence or look up every word. Focus on understanding the general meaning and becoming comfortable with natural English. Start shorter if an hour feels heavy and build consistency.

modules.title: Pronunciation — Word Endings
modules.reason: Make final consonants, plural endings and -ed endings audible.
modules.checkpoint: Produce the target endings clearly in at least 8 out of 10 items.

items.title: Review final-sound routine
items.description: Before practice, say the target plural, -ed and final-consonant endings slowly and clearly. Focus on making the final sound audible.

items.title: Apply endings in Read Aloud
items.description: Complete 3 new Read Aloud attempts while protecting final consonants and grammatical endings.

modules.title: Pronunciation — Problem Sounds
modules.reason: Work on the specific consonant or vowel contrast that is reducing clarity.
modules.checkpoint: Produce the target sound clearly in at least 8 out of 10 items.

items.title: Review the target sound
items.description: Use the exact sound pair identified by your teacher. Say each sound slowly, then use it in short words and sentences.

items.title: Apply the target sound in speaking
items.description: Complete 3 new Read Aloud attempts while monitoring the target sound.

modules.title: Fluency — Chunking
modules.reason: Develop smoother phrasing by speaking in meaningful groups of words.
modules.checkpoint: Produce three smooth recordings with sensible chunking.

items.title: Chunking practice — Read Aloud
items.description: Complete 5 new Read Aloud attempts. Before each attempt, mentally group the text into meaningful phrases rather than reading word-by-word.

items.title: Review the shadowing routine
items.description: After listening to a clear model outside the timed task, imitate its phrase groups and rhythm before repeating without the model.

modules.title: Fluency — Pauses & Recovery
modules.reason: Keep speaking after small errors instead of stopping and restarting.
modules.checkpoint: Complete three timed attempts without disruptive pauses.

items.title: Pause-and-recovery practice
items.description: Complete 3 new Describe Image attempts. If you make a small mistake, continue instead of restarting the sentence.

modules.title: Fluency — Pace
modules.reason: Maintain a steady pace without rushing or slowing excessively.
modules.checkpoint: Maintain a steady, understandable pace in three recordings.

items.title: Controlled pace practice
items.description: Complete 3 new Read Aloud attempts at a steady, understandable pace. Avoid rushing to finish early.

modules.title: Content Picking — Main Idea
modules.reason: Identify the central idea before adding supporting information.
modules.checkpoint: Identify the correct central idea in at least 4 out of 5 attempts.

items.title: Main idea method
items.description: First identify the topic, then ask what the writer or speaker is mainly saying about that topic. Use task-specific practice assigned by your teacher; for SWT content problems, use the Highlight Trainer.

modules.title: Content Picking — Prioritisation
modules.reason: Separate essential information from examples and minor details.
modules.checkpoint: Select concise, relevant information in at least 4 out of 5 attempts.

items.title: Prioritisation method
items.description: Separate essential ideas from examples, repetition and minor detail. For SWT, use the Highlight Trainer so the portal can check your selections.

modules.title: SWT — Context Accuracy
modules.reason: Preserve the original relationship between ideas, including cause, contrast and viewpoint.
modules.checkpoint: Produce at least 4 out of 5 summaries without changing the source meaning.

items.title: SWT context-accuracy practice
items.description: Complete 5 new SWT attempts. After each response, compare whether cause, contrast, viewpoint and conclusion still match the source.

modules.title: Describe Image — Topic, Key Features & Trends
modules.reason: Identify what the image is about and report the strongest features instead of trying to describe everything.
modules.checkpoint: Complete 5 Describe Image attempts with a clear topic and several meaningful features delivered confidently.

items.title: Use a flexible structure, not a fixed template
items.description: Introduce the image type and topic, then report key features such as highest, lowest, major comparisons, increases or decreases. Mention the x- and y-axes only when useful. A separate conclusion is optional if the key content is already clear.

items.title: Prioritise the strongest features
items.description: You cannot cover everything in the available time. Focus on the main topic, major trends and a few reportable features. Do not rush just to list every number.

items.title: Describe Image content practice
items.description: Complete 5 new Describe Image attempts. Before speaking, identify the image type, topic and 3–4 strongest features or trends.

modules.title: Note-Taking — Useful Meaning, Not Maximum Writing
modules.reason: Capture enough meaning to reconstruct important ideas without letting note-taking replace listening.
modules.checkpoint: Capture the main topic and important support while staying with the audio.

items.title: Choose note length based on your memory
items.description: If you can reconstruct ideas from keywords, use short notes. If you rely heavily on notes, write longer meaningful phrases. Do not spend time writing filler or examples. Abbreviate easy words when useful, but make sure important phrases are complete enough to understand later.

items.title: Retell Lecture note-taking practice
items.description: Complete 5 new Retell Lecture attempts. First understand the topic, then capture useful support without stopping to perfect every note.

modules.title: SGD — Speaker Tracking & Third-Person Summary
modules.reason: Capture the overall topic and each speaker's useful contribution without mixing speakers or reproducing every turn chronologically.
modules.checkpoint: Complete 5 discussions with clear S1/S2/S3 attribution and connected third-person reporting.

items.title: Organise notes by speaker
items.description: Keep separate S1 / S2 / S3 areas. Capture the overall topic and about 2–3 useful ideas from each speaker where available. Do not stop listening to perfect one note; capture keywords or short phrases and build complete sentences later.

items.title: Report in third person
items.description: Group each speaker's ideas together instead of going back and forth in the original order. Use third person: 'he said', 'she mentioned', 'the second speaker explained'. If voices sound similar, distinguish speakers by their ideas.

items.title: SGD speaker-tracking practice
items.description: Complete 5 new Summarize Group Discussion attempts. Avoid mixing speakers, fragmented sentences, excessive fillers and unreadable notes.

modules.title: Note-Taking — Speed
modules.reason: Use abbreviations and symbols so notes do not fall behind the audio.
modules.checkpoint: Capture the main idea and support while keeping pace with the audio.

items.title: Note-taking speed practice
items.description: Complete 5 new Retell Lecture attempts using abbreviations, arrows and content words so you can keep pace with the audio.

modules.title: Grammar — Sentence Building
modules.reason: Connect important ideas accurately using controlled clauses.
modules.checkpoint: Produce at least 4 out of 5 structurally accurate sentences.

items.title: Sentence-building method
items.description: Practise joining 2–3 related ideas while preserving their logical relationship. Your teacher can add exact SWT, SST or Essay questions to this plan for scored practice.

modules.title: Grammar — Run-ons & Punctuation
modules.reason: Control long sentences and clause boundaries.
modules.checkpoint: Produce at least 4 out of 5 controlled sentences without run-ons.

items.title: Run-on repair method
items.description: Before full PTE practice, check clause boundaries: each added idea needs a clear grammatical relationship and controlled punctuation.

modules.title: Vocabulary — Collocations
modules.reason: Learn common word combinations rather than isolated vocabulary.
modules.checkpoint: Reach at least 80% across three practice sets.

items.title: Build a collocation notebook
items.description: Record the full phrase, meaning and one example sentence instead of learning isolated words.

items.title: Reading Blanks collocation practice
items.description: Complete 3 new Reading Blanks (Dropdown) questions and review which word combinations fit the surrounding context.

modules.title: Comprehension — Distractors
modules.reason: Use evidence to separate the best answer from plausible distractors.
modules.checkpoint: Answer at least 4 out of 5 questions correctly and explain the evidence.

items.title: Reading distractor practice
items.description: Complete 5 new Reading Single Answer questions. For each, identify the evidence for the correct option and why the distractors are weaker.

modules.title: Spelling — Personal Error Log
modules.reason: Target the spelling mistakes you personally repeat.
modules.checkpoint: Reach at least 90% on your personal error list twice.

items.title: Build your spelling error log
items.description: Record repeated spelling errors with the corrected form and one short example.

items.title: Retest your error list
items.description: After 2–3 days, cover the correct forms and retest the same words. Keep errors that still repeat.

modules.title: Repeat Sentence — Capture More Correct Content
modules.reason: Reproduce as much correct content as possible and train on sentences that genuinely challenge your memory.
modules.checkpoint: Complete 5 challenging Repeat Sentence attempts and increase the amount of correct content you can reproduce.

items.title: Capture more, not random words
items.description: Try to reproduce as much of the sentence as you can accurately. Do not give up early after a few words. More correct content is useful; extra guessed or unrelated words are not.

items.title: Practise difficult sentences
items.description: Do not practise only easy Repeat Sentence items. Use longer or more difficult sentences regularly so memory, listening retention and sentence reconstruction improve.

items.title: Repeat Sentence challenge set
items.description: Complete 5 new Repeat Sentence attempts, prioritising difficult items and trying to reproduce more correct content on each attempt.

modules.title: Listening Memory — Word Order
modules.reason: Retain sentence order, articles, prepositions and other small words.
modules.checkpoint: Retain order and key function words in at least 4 out of 5 sentences.

items.title: Write From Dictation reconstruction practice
items.description: Complete 5 new Write From Dictation attempts and check word order, articles, prepositions and endings.

modules.title: Respond to a Situation — Natural First-Person Response
modules.reason: Match the greeting and tone to the listener, turn the prompt into first person and complete the communication goal naturally.
modules.checkpoint: Complete 5 situations where the audience, reason, request and closing are all clear.

items.title: Respond to a Situation — Exercise 1
items.description: Watch how the response identifies the audience, purpose and appropriate wording.

items.title: Respond to a Situation — Exercise 2
items.description: Watch, then apply the same audience-and-purpose thinking to a new situation.

items.title: Greeting → situation → request → closing
items.description: Known person: use a natural greeting such as 'Hi [name]'. Unknown person: use a neutral polite greeting such as 'Hello' or 'Excuse me'. Group: use 'Hello everyone'. Then explain the situation in first person, add a realistic relevant detail, make the required request or suggestion, and close politely.

items.title: Do not repeat the prompt mechanically
items.description: Convert the situation into natural speech. You may make vague details specific—for example, 'unforeseen circumstances' can become illness or an appointment—provided the detail is realistic, relevant and does not contradict the prompt.

items.title: Respond to a Situation practice
items.description: Complete 5 new Respond to a Situation attempts. Before speaking, identify who you are talking to, what happened and exactly what you need to say or ask.

modules.title: SWT Content Selection — Highlight Trainer
modules.reason: Practise deciding what belongs in the summary before worrying about sentence writing.
modules.checkpoint: Complete at least 10 existing-passage selection exercises and review every missed central idea.

items.title: Highlight the important phrases — 15 exercises
items.description: Use existing SWT passages. Drag over only the words and phrases that carry the central message or essential support. After each submission, the trainer shows what you missed, why it matters, and the central phrases. No full summary writing.

modules.weakness: Task method, content selection and synthesis
modules.title: SWT — Main Idea, Support & Synthesis
modules.reason: Select the right ideas first, preserve their relationships and meaning, then connect them in one controlled sentence.
modules.checkpoint: Complete 4 out of 5 SWT responses with a clear main idea, relevant support, preserved meaning and valid form.

items.title: Review SWT form
items.description: Keep SWT as one sentence and within 5–75 words. Do not force an artificial 60–65 word target; preserve important meaning while staying inside the valid form.

items.title: Identify the topic and what happens to it
items.description: Scan the whole passage. Repeated keywords often reveal the main topic; then ask what the passage is actually saying about that topic. Use What, Why and How to find the important support and turning points.

items.title: Choose relevant support
items.description: Keep ideas that directly explain the main topic, important turning points and the conclusion where one exists. Avoid examples, detailed explanations, repeated information and unnecessary dates or 'when' details.

items.title: No rigid SWT template
items.description: Use suitable wording from the passage when helpful. Connect 3–4 important ideas with accurate academic connectives such as moreover, furthermore, however, therefore, whereas, additionally, in addition or hence. Do not force beginning/middle/end selection or an artificial 60–65 word target.

items.title: Compress wording, not meaning
items.description: If the response is too long, do not delete an important idea just to reduce words. Synthesize it with fewer words or connect it to another related idea while preserving the meaning.

items.title: Use the Highlight Trainer for content selection
items.description: If choosing important lines is difficult, complete the SWT Content Selection — Highlight Trainer before full SWT writing.

items.title: Full SWT application
items.description: Complete 3 new SWT attempts. Read the final sentence once for connection, relevance, preserved meaning and missing grammar components.

modules.title: Timing & Preparation
modules.reason: Apply a known strategy reliably within PTE timing.
modules.checkpoint: Complete at least 4 out of 5 attempts within the required timing.

items.title: Three-stage timing routine
items.description: Do the same task once untimed, once with reduced preparation time, and then under full test timing. Your teacher can attach exact questions for this routine.

modules.title: SST — Understand First, Then Note
modules.reason: Understand the audio first, capture the topic, strong supporting ideas and conclusion, then turn notes into a connected summary.
modules.checkpoint: Complete 4 out of 5 SST attempts with a clear topic, relevant support, connected meaning and controlled spelling.

items.title: How to Attempt Summarise Spoken Text
items.description: Watch the task method before practising.

items.title: Listen before writing everything
items.description: Do not automatically write from the first word. First identify the real topic. Ignore filler introductions, examples, repetition and minor detail. Aim for the main topic, about two important supporting ideas and the conclusion where it exists.

items.title: Use notes that work for you
items.description: If you rely heavily on notes, write longer meaningful phrases. If your listening retention is stronger, shorter keywords and your own abbreviations are fine. Do not force a keyword-only strategy on every student. Complete important ideas and repair fragmented notes from memory before writing.

items.title: Flexible SST structure
items.description: Use the IPT structure as a guide, not a rigid formula: 'The speaker discussed...' followed by suitable connectors such as Moreover, However, Firstly, Furthermore, Secondly, Additionally, Therefore, Lastly or In conclusion. Use 'and' or 'but' only when the ideas genuinely connect that way.

items.title: SST scored application
items.description: Complete 3 new Summarize Spoken Text attempts. Prioritise connected content first, then spelling and minor grammar refinements.

modules.title: Essay Writing — Core Method
modules.reason: Understand the prompt, plan a clear response, develop relevant ideas and meet the essay scoring requirements.
modules.checkpoint: Complete an essay that addresses the prompt, meets form requirements and shows clear development and organisation.

items.title: Analyse the essay prompt
items.description: Identify exactly what the prompt asks you to discuss, compare, explain or evaluate. Give an explicit opinion only when the prompt asks for one.

items.title: Plan before writing
items.description: Prepare two relevant body ideas and the supporting explanation/examples you will use.

items.title: Essay scored application
items.description: Complete 2 new Essay attempts after planning. Progress updates automatically after the essay review is saved.

modules.title: Read Aloud — Natural Pace & Pausing
modules.reason: Read clearly at a moderate pace and use punctuation to guide natural pauses.
modules.checkpoint: Complete 5 Read Aloud attempts without rushing, dragging or sounding word-by-word.

items.title: Use punctuation as your pause guide
items.description: Do not speak too fast or too slowly. Read at a moderate pace. Take a short natural pause at commas and a clearer pause at sentence endings. Do not force dramatic intonation; if the listener can understand you easily, the delivery is working.

items.title: Read Aloud pace practice
items.description: Complete 5 new Read Aloud attempts. Focus on clear words, a moderate pace and natural pauses instead of maximum speed.

modules.title: Retell Lecture — Main Idea to Conclusion
modules.reason: Capture the main topic, two strong supporting ideas and the conclusion, then retell them confidently.
modules.checkpoint: Complete 5 Retell Lecture attempts with a clear topic, relevant support and a connected ending.

items.title: Retell Lecture content structure
items.description: Listen for the main topic, then capture about two important supporting ideas and the conclusion where one exists. Do not read disconnected notes aloud. Reconstruct incomplete notes from memory and connect them into meaningful ideas.

items.title: Flexible linking phrases
items.description: Use phrases such as 'Moreover, he also discussed...', 'Furthermore, he talked about...', 'He also emphasized...' and 'In conclusion...' only when they fit. The content controls the response; the phrases only help organise it.

items.title: Retell Lecture application
items.description: Complete 5 new Retell Lecture attempts. Keep the response confident, connected and focused on the lecture's important content.
